title: Upstreaming speculation rules and prefetch to HTML
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Chromium has been developing and specifying various speculative loading features over in https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation.

Recently, Mozilla expressed interest in seeing a subset of these upstreamed to HTML: see https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/620#issuecomment-2703979191 and preceding comments. We're very excited to work on this from the Chromium side, although it might take a quarter to shift around engineering resources before we start really making active progress.

This issue is for tracking and planning that work. A tentative plan, very open to feedback:

- The initial target is [speculation rules](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html) and [prefetch](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html)
  - We would omit prerender-specific pieces for now, e.g. the prefetch + prerender integration parts of the prefetch spec, and the prerender type in the speculation rules spec.
    - (Or maybe we should include the prerender type but allow it to trigger prefetch behavior?)
- We should fix all relevant issues tagged [needs spec edits](https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22needs%20spec%20edits%22) and [bug](https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3Abug) before the upstreaming.
  - Most of these are around service worker integration, and Chromium is working through them now as we implement service worker + prefetch support.
- Similar to the discussion in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7533, we can add a specific carveout to allow browser UI to trigger prefetching, separate from speculation rules.
